pr.title: Show saved artifacts in the session panel
pr.head: dff64381c6dac4d999183b5a5b4e6e0596e79ff0

summary: An artifact is a saved static HTML bundle with immutable versions. This change gives those bundles a place in each session panel, so their links remain findable after a conversation scrolls past them.

Open chooses the configured Projector site for published content or extracts a temporary loopback preview. Dismiss hides one artifact in one session without deleting a version or changing another session. A new version keeps the dismissal until you restore it.

The review requests changes for two Open failures: the terminal drawer does not display a fallback link when browser opening fails, and directory redirects in a local preview lose the token in the URL.

cards.title: The saved records
cards.html:
• Artifact ID: the stable lowercase name across versions.
  • Version: a digest of the manifest and exact asset bytes.
  • Catalog: metadata read from cached Git refs, without fetching payloads.
  • Preview token: a random path prefix checked by the temporary loopback server.

cards.title: Validation and limits
cards.html:
• The required gate passed, including 267 hook tests and CI.
  • All 117 focused Python tests passed.
  • The live desktop and phone browser check passed; both screenshots were inspected.
  • Two isolated reproductions confirmed the open P2 findings.
  • Large existing console, hook, and CLI modules were read through changed sections and affected callers.

groups.title: Expose artifact actions to both hosts
groups.kicker: The CLI and host types agree on metadata and actions.
intro: The panel needs a small metadata record rather than an artifact payload. The CLI adds list, open, dismiss, and restore commands; the hook parser accepts only rows with the fields its renderer consumes.

The list command takes a session ID so visibility is specific to that session. Open takes the checkout, remote, and stable artifact ID, leaving the version selection and preview decision in the shared Python layer.

groups.title: Cache metadata and serve a local preview
groups.kicker: Discover saved bundles without repeatedly loading their files.
intro: The catalog caches metadata by the tips of the fetched remote ref and local artifact ref. It reads latest pointers and manifests, gives local versions precedence, and skips invalid entries. A dismissal records the checkout, remote, and artifact ID as a stable key, so another revision does not make the row reappear.

Open uses the configured site when hosting is confirmed. Otherwise it validates and extracts the saved bundle, starts a loopback server under a random URL prefix, reuses a live preview for the same version, and removes extracted files when the preview expires.

files.note: Adds the cached catalog, per-session dismissal store, hosted-link decision, and expiring preview server.

checks.text: Focused tests checked that catalog refresh reads metadata without payloads, unchanged refs reuse the cache, dismissal survives a revision, and previews preserve binary bytes and expire.

A relative link to a directory without a trailing slash redirects after the token is stripped. The Location becomes /docs/ rather than /<token>/docs/, so following it returns 404. A disposable preview reproduced the failure.

groups.title: Keep artifact rows available in session panels
groups.kicker: Poll the catalog and attach Open and Dismiss controls.
intro: The Claude Code panel polls artifact metadata alongside its existing content, counts artifacts in the header, and expands each row into its description and controls. A revision guard prevents a catalog read that started before Dismiss from putting that row back.

The terminal console includes artifacts in each session panel and rereads persisted dismissals when applying a refresh. The managed console extends the same path to durable sessions, including stopped ones; an artifact action remains separate from native agent handoff.

groups.title: Check persistence, races, and hosted content
groups.kicker: Exercise the new panel behavior and record the deferred live check.
intro: The regression tests use temporary Git repositories for real saved versions and local preview processes. They cover per-session visibility, revision persistence, cached metadata, preview reuse and expiry, binary assets, host checks, console actions, and a refresh that completes after dismissal.

The live browser script selects the cache-explorer fixture by ID so unrelated published artifacts do not invalidate the check. It still exercises both saved versions, navigation, assets, keyboard controls, search, and full-screen behavior at desktop and phone sizes.
